newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan Taleban said in peace talks with rivals.
newsitem.headline: Afghan Taleban said in peace talks with rivals.

text.p: Afghanistan's Taleban Islamic militia is holding peace talks with the opponents who drove it out of the northern city of Mazar-i-Sharif, a Pakistan Foreign Ministry spokesman said on Thursday.

The spokesman, quoting reports received in Islamabad, told reporters that "negotiations are currently under way in Afghanistan to remove differences among various groups". He declined to give details, saying that would amount to interference in Afghan affairs.

Pakistan was the first country to recognise the Taleban government in Afghanistan after the purist Ismamic militia captured Mazar-i-Sharif, the main opposition stronghold in the north, on Saturday and has a consulate in the city.
The spokesman said Pakistan's information was that "there were some differences" that led to the latest fighting between the Taleban and its new ally, Uzbek General Abdul Malik.

"They are talking to each other now," he said. Also involved in the talks was the opposition Hezb-i-Wahdat faction of Shi'ite Moslems, who fought along Malik's forces to drive out the Taleban from Mazar-i-Sharif.
